developments.title: BoJ holds 1.25%; target-consistent inflation and conditional tightening remain active
developments.facts: Official decision: 8-1 hold around 1.25%; Takata preferred 1.50% and faster movement toward neutral. Complete Bank View judges underlying CPI generally consistent with 2%, conditions accommodative, and says the Bank will continue raising rates while considering timing/pace against outlook and risks. FY2026/27/28 GDP medians 0.7/0.7/0.8%, changes +0.1/-0.1/0.0 points versus July. Ex-fresh-food CPI 2.5/2.6/2.0%, changes 0.0/+0.2/0.0; ex-fresh-food/energy 2.4/2.7/2.3%, changes -0.1/+0.1/+0.1. Activity risk balanced, price risk upward. Tight labour and wage-price interaction coexist with roughly flat near-term consumption, declining housing and energy/terms-of-trade pressure. Forecasts exclude proposed food-tax cut; possible FY2027 mechanical CPI effect around -1.3 points if implemented is not delivered disinflation. Unanimous ETF annual sales pace rises JPY 330 bn to JPY 860 bn book value from January 2027, about JPY 2460 bn market-value equivalent, with adjustment/suspension flexibility; J-REIT pace remains about JPY 5 bn. One policy package, not independent votes. Hold, target recognition and higher next-year inflation were broadly anticipated in the Reuters preview; no surprise December commitment or measured repricing claimed. Governor conference remains pending.

direction.reason: Moderate strengthening retained after completed Ueda Q&A and a fresh contrary review. Expected1.25% hold alone is not the signal: target-consistent underlying inflation, broadening consumer-price pressure and continuing adjustment towards neutral support prospective yield incentives; non-dollar haven/lower-US-yield conditions reinforce this. No fixed hike interval, no sharply greater upside risk than a month ago, cumulative tightening lags, uncertain neutral rate and next wage bargaining cap confidence. December is possible and already widely anticipated, not promised. Weak housing/retail and oil-import costs oppose strength. Grade reflects policy and haven mechanisms, not the chart or measured OIS repricing. JPY has more domestic normalisation support than CHF at0%; GBP/NZD are less insulated from risk. A patient BoJ, restored US yield advantage or risk recovery defeats the case. The full Outlook is the next scheduled domestic information stage; Bank View already known is not treated as fresh. Daly introductory role does not leave Ueda unresolved; no USDJPY entry is renewed while actual Musalem guidance is unavailable.
